CYBERPUNK.DodgeText: -2 to attackers' hit rolls. You get -3 to your actions while dodging.

CYBERPUNK.HoldText: Succeed? Opponent immobilized until escape made.

CYBERPUNK.MartialFxThrowBody: {target} is knocked prone by Throw. Must spend one action to stand up before acting normally. (CP2020 p.100)
CYBERPUNK.MartialFxSweepBody: {target} is knocked prone by Sweep/Trip. Must spend one action to stand up before acting normally. (CP2020 p.100)
CYBERPUNK.MartialFxHeldBody: {target} is held by {attacker}. Target can only attempt Escape (contested roll). (CP2020 p.100)
CYBERPUNK.MartialFxGrappledBody: {target} is grappled by {attacker}. Grapple: attacker can Hold, Choke, or Throw on subsequent turns as a free action. (CP2020 p.100–102)
CYBERPUNK.MartialFxChokeBody: {target} is being choked by {attacker}. Takes 1d6 damage per turn and must pass Stun Save each turn or fall unconscious. (CP2020 p.100)
CYBERPUNK.DodgeHint: Defensive: incoming melee attacks take -2 to hit this turn. You're at -3 to your own actions while dodging.
CYBERPUNK.BlockParryHint: Defensive: block or parry an incoming melee attack outright — no damage if you win the contest. Blades must save or break. -3 to your actions while blocking.
CYBERPUNK.StrikeHint: Punch attack — 1D3 + STR damage bonus + martial-art bonus. Contested vs the target's defense.
CYBERPUNK.KickHint: Kick attack — 1D6 + STR damage bonus + martial-art bonus. Hits harder than a strike. Contested.
CYBERPUNK.DisarmHint: Knock the target's weapon out of their hands on a successful contested roll.
CYBERPUNK.SweepTripHint: Knock the target prone: -2 to their next attack, +2 to yours. They must spend an action to stand.
CYBERPUNK.GrappleHint: Grab the target. While grappled you can Hold, Choke, or Throw them as a free action on later turns.
CYBERPUNK.HoldHint: Immobilize a grabbed target until they break free with Escape.
CYBERPUNK.ChokeHint: Strangle a held target: 1D6 damage per turn, and they must pass a Stun Save each turn or fall unconscious.
CYBERPUNK.ThrowHint: Throw the target down: 1D6 + STR damage and knocked prone (they must spend an action to stand).
CYBERPUNK.EscapeHint: Break free from an opponent's Hold or Grapple on a successful contested roll.
CYBERPUNK.PunchHint: Basic punch — 1D3 + STR damage bonus + martial-art bonus. Contested melee strike.
CYBERPUNK.RamHint: FNFF2: charging body-slam — drive into the target with your momentum.
CYBERPUNK.JumpKickHint: FNFF2: leaping kick — higher damage than a standard kick.
CYBERPUNK.CastHint: FNFF2: a throwing maneuver — hurl the opponent using their own momentum.
CYBERPUNK.AllOutParryHint: FNFF2: commit your whole turn to parrying for a strong defensive bonus — you can't attack.
CYBERPUNK.AllOutDodgeHint: FNFF2: commit your whole turn to dodging for a strong defensive bonus — you can't attack.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoTrackingHint: When on, weapons can't fire on an empty magazine — reload to draw from linked ammo. Turn off for Free Fire (ammo ignored, infinite reloads).
CYBERPUNK.SuppressiveDesc: Each creature inside or crossing the fire-zone rolls Athletics + REF + 1d10 vs DC ({save}).
CYBERPUNK.SuppressiveHitsDesc: On failure the target suffers 1D6 hits; each hit deals {dmg} damage to a random location.
CYBERPUNK.ReputationHint: Your social standing (CP2020 p.54). GM-set; can be negative for cowardice/infamy. Feeds the Facedown and Recognition rolls.
CYBERPUNK.FacedownHint: Roll 1d10 + COOL + Reputation. Target one foe's token first to make it a contested Facedown.
CYBERPUNK.FacedownSoloHint: Target one foe's token to make this a contested Facedown.
CYBERPUNK.FacedownPenalty: {loser} backs down — or is at −3 vs {winner} until they win a Facedown against them. (GM enforces.)
CYBERPUNK.FacedownTie: Tie — neither side backs down; no penalty.
CYBERPUNK.RecognitionHint: Roll 1d10 vs your Reputation: at or under = they recognize you; over = they haven't heard of you.
CYBERPUNK.RecognizedNo: Not recognized — rolled {roll} > Rep {rep}. They haven't heard of {name}.
CYBERPUNK.UnderThresholdMessage: Roll under the thresholds to succeed

CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.AcpaCheckboxTip: Powered Armor (ACPA). Uncheck to turn this back into a standard vehicle (the sheet switches automatically).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.AcpaPoweredArmorTip: Powered Armor (ACPA): derives Body Value from chassis STR ÷ 20 instead of SDP, has equal armor on every facing, takes no size penalty to be hit, and includes a built-in vehicle link (Maximum Metal, p.52).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ControlRollTipAcpa: Roll a Control / Maneuver check (REF + Pilot + 1d10 vs Difficulty Value). On failure, rolls the loss/failure table for the active ruleset.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ControlRollTipVehicle: Roll a Control / Maneuver check (REF + Driving/Pilot + 1d10 vs Difficulty Value). On failure, rolls the Control Loss / Failure table for the active ruleset.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.DamageTipAcpa: Resolve damage against this suit. Maximum Metal compares Penetration to Armor Value, then rolls the powered-armor System Hit / Critical Hit / Integrity flow.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.DamageTipVehicle: Resolve damage against this vehicle. Core subtracts SP and reduces SDP; Maximum Metal compares Penetration to Armor Value, rolls Surface/Minor/Major/Catastrophic and a hit location with fuel-fire / ammo-cookoff / crew effects.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.MeleeTip: ACPA hand-to-hand (Maximum Metal p.58): Punch / Crush / Kick → vehicle-scale Penetration through the dispatcher. Target a token first.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.RepairTip: Field repair: restore the suit to full — frame SOP per area, SDP, power, and clear all damage/status.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ChassisStrTip: Chassis Strength (Linear Frame). Drives Body Value (STR ÷ 20), melee damage and lift (Maximum Metal p.5/61).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.BodyValueTip: Body Value = chassis STR ÷ 20 (rounded). Subtracted on the MM damage-severity roll. Read-only.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ArmorSpTip: Armor-shell Stopping Power. ACPA armor is equal on every side (no flank rules); SP ≤ 2× chassis STR (MM p.61).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ArmorValueTipAcpa: Armor Value = SP ÷ 20 (MM p.4). A weapon's Penetration is compared to this. Read-only.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SdpCurrentTip: Structural Damage Points — the suit's structural hit points.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SpFrontTip: Stopping Power — the vehicle's armor. Core subtracts SP from incoming damage (p.112); Maximum Metal instead converts it to Armor Value (SP ÷ 20).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.AvFrontTip: Armor Value = SP ÷ 20 (Maximum Metal, p.4). A weapon's Penetration is compared to this value — not to raw SP — to see if it gets through. Read-only; edit SP to change it.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.FacingSpTip: Per-facing armor (Maximum Metal flank rules, p.4): a hit to the side uses 75% of armor, top/rear/bottom 50%. The facing depends on the angle of the shot. ACPA armor is equal on all sides.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SdpCurrentVehicleTip: Structural Damage Points — the vehicle's hit points. Damage that gets past SP comes off here; at 0 SDP the vehicle is destroyed / inoperable (Core p.112).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SdpMaxVehicleTip: Maximum SDP — the undamaged total. Body Value is derived from this.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.BodyValueVehicleTip: Body Value = SDP ÷ 20 (rounded), or chassis STR ÷ 20 for ACPA. The vehicle's bulk/toughness on the Maximum Metal damage scale (p.4): it is subtracted on the damage-severity roll. Every vehicle has one (e.g. SDP 50 → Body 3); Core mode just doesn't use it — it tracks raw SDP instead. Read-only.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ChassisStrVehicleTip: ACPA chassis Strength. For powered armor, Body Value is STR ÷ 20 instead of SDP ÷ 20 (Maximum Metal, p.5).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.StrDamageTip: Suit Strength lost to Critical Hits (reduces melee damage and lift). 0 = undamaged.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.RefDamageTip: Suit Reflexes lost to Critical Hits (reduces the pilot's REF / control). 0 = undamaged.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.PowerHrsTip: Remaining power-cell life in hours (24h normal). Drained by power-unit criticals.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.CoolingMinTipAcpa: Minutes until heatstroke after a cooling-system critical (0 = OK). Counts down ~0.05/round (3s rounds); at 0 the heatstroke escalation begins.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.CoolingMinTipVehicle: Minutes until heatstroke after a cooling-system critical (0 = OK). When it expires the pilot makes escalating Stun Saves.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.HeatstrokeTip: Heatstroke escalation after the cooling build-up expires (MM p.55): 0 none · 1 Serious · 2 Critical · 3 Mortal · 4 out. The pilot makes a Stun/Shock Save one level worse each round.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.InterfaceOutTip: Rounds the interface/electronics are out (counts down each combat round).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SeizedRdsTipAcpa: Rounds a body area is seized up / immobile (counts down each round; mobility restored at 0).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SeizedRdsTipVehicle: Rounds a body area is seized up / immobile (counts down each combat round; restores mobility at 0).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.TopSpeedTip: Maximum speed. In Maximum Metal, going fast costs handling: the maneuver Difficulty rises +1 for every 10% of top speed you are driving above 50% of top speed (p.11).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SafeSpeedTip: The fastest you can go without a handling penalty. In Core, driving at 2× / 3× / 4× safe speed applies −2 / −4 / −6 to the Control Roll (p.112).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.AccelerationTip: How much speed the vehicle can gain per combat turn (Maximum Metal chase rules).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.DecelerationTip: How much speed the vehicle can shed per combat turn — braking (Maximum Metal chase rules).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ControlModTip: Vehicle handling modifier added to every Control / Maneuver roll (e.g. sportscar +2, limo −3, truck −4). It prefills the Control Roll dialog. Core uses the p.112 table; Maximum Metal the revised p.11 table.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.CrewSlotsTip: How many crew positions the vehicle has (driver, gunner, etc.). At least one is needed to operate it.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.PassengerSlotsTip: How many additional passengers the vehicle can carry beyond the crew.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.VehicleLinkTip: Cybernetic vehicle link: the driver/pilot adds +2 to all control, maneuver, and vehicle-weapon rolls, and can act while driving without the 'doing something else' penalty (Maximum Metal). ACPA always counts as linked.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.DamageControlTip: A redundant network of backups, fire extinguishers and breakers. When a system is hit, roll 1d10 — on a 6-10 it keeps working as if undamaged (Maximum Metal, p.4). Used by the damage resolver.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.DamageControlTipAcpa: Damage Control: a hit system keeps working on a 1d10 of 6-10 (MM p.4).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.CompositeArmorTip: Composite armor (metals + plastics + ceramics + depleted heavy metals): halves the Penetration of shaped-charge HEAT weapons, but penetrating damage is not halved (Maximum Metal, p.23). Used by the damage resolver.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.CompositeArmorTipAcpa: Composite armor: halves shaped-charge (HEAT) Penetration (MM p.23).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ReactiveArmorTip: Reactive armor: explosive tiles that detonate against shaped-charge (HEAT) attacks. On a HEAT hit, roll 1d10 — 2-10 halves Penetration, minus 1 per two prior shaped-charge / high-explosive hits the array has absorbed. Tiles are consumed each hit; press Replace to rearm after a battle (Maximum Metal, p.23). Stacks with Composite (¼ Pen if both fire). Used by the damage resolver.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ReactiveWearTip: Shaped-charge / high-explosive hits absorbed by the reactive tiles. The deflection roll drops 1 for every two hits. Replace rearms the array (resets wear to 0).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ReactiveReplaceTip: Rearm the reactive array (reset wear to 0)
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SensorsRadarTip: Sensors / radar: automatically detect an inbound missile (90%) so the crew can react. Without sensors, detection falls back to a Notice/Awareness roll (Maximum Metal, p.10/25-26).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.AntiMissileTip: Anti-missile system (AGAMS/AEAMS): when a missile is detected, the crew may attempt to shoot it down — destroy on a roll of 4+, detonate it early (half damage) on 1-3 (Maximum Metal, p.24).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.AntiMissileTipAcpa: Anti-missile (AGAMS): may shoot down a detected missile.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.FireControlTipVehicle: Targeting-computer bonus added to the vehicle's weapon to-hit rolls (Maximum Metal). 0 = no fire-control computer.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.FireControlTipAcpa: Targeting-computer / fire-control bonus added to weapon to-hit rolls.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ToughnessTip: Toughness Mod (MM p.62): reduces incoming damage (like BTM). Derived from chassis STR. Read-only.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.FrameDamModTip: Linear-frame melee Damage Mod (frame worn standalone; full ACPA melee uses Punch/Crush/Kick). Derived.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.LiftKgTip: Dead-weight lift (kg), derived from chassis STR.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.CarryKgTip: Carry capacity (kg), derived from chassis STR.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.FrameSopNote: Frame SOP per body area (max, from chassis STR — Head/Arm 25%, Leg 50%, Torso 75%). Destroying an area kills its systems; the Torso shuts the suit down.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.RealityInterfaceTip: Reality Interface (MM p.64). Always mounted in the helmet. Sets the suit's SIB contribution and its Direct-Fire Bonus (DFB) — the to-hit modifier when the suit fires its own weapons, replacing any smartgun bonus.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ReflexControlTip: Reflex/Control system (MM p.65). Sets the REF modifier and the maximum operating Reflex (the suit's REF cap). Takes no spaces. Advanced is the free military standard.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.DfbToHitTip: Direct-Fire Bonus — added to the suit's weapon to-hit rolls (replaces any smartgun bonus). Derived from the Reality Interface. Read-only.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.InterfaceSibTip: The Reality Interface's contribution to the suit's Initiative Bonus (SIB). Derived. Read-only.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.MaxRefTip: Maximum operating Reflex allowed by the Reflex/Control system. The pilot's REF is capped here while driving the suit. Read-only.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.PilotLinkTip: Link the pilot character actor. Its REF drives the suit's effective REF, and it takes frame-breach / overflow damage (firing the normal stun/death saves). Leave as (none) to use the manual Pilot REF.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.LinkedPilotRefTip: The linked pilot's base REF (from their character sheet), used as the suit's base REF.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.PilotRefManualTip: Manual fallback base Reflex (REF), used when no pilot actor is linked.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.EffectiveRefTip: Effective operating REF = clamp(pilot REF + Reflex/Control mod, 0..max) − suit REF critical damage. Derived. Read-only.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.CommandComputerTip: Command & Control Computer (C3): squad-coordination option, +1 to Initiative and Awareness while linked. Integrable with any Reflex/Control system.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SibNote: Suit Initiative Bonus (SIB) = round(chassis Lift/Cap ÷ total loaded weight) − 1, plus the Reality Interface SIB. Total weight = chassis + armor shell + Trooper capacity + interface + systems.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SibInitiativeTip: Suit Initiative Bonus (SIB) — added to the pilot's initiative in ACPA combat. Derived from the power-to-weight ratio + the Reality Interface. Read-only.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.TotalWtKgTip: Total fully-loaded weight (kg). Derived; drives the SIB. Read-only.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ArmorWtKgTip: Armor-shell weight (kg), from the chosen shell SP via the Armor Inventory Table. Derived. Read-only.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.TrooperCapTip: Trooper Capacity — the weight budget set aside for the pilot and personal gear (counts toward total weight for SIB). 114 kg standard; Russian frames 136; elite 80-91.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ExtraSysWtTip: EXTRA / misc systems weight (kg) added ON TOP of the mounted-systems weight (shown in the Systems section). Mounted acpaSystem Items are summed automatically; use this only for gear not in the catalog. Both count toward Total Weight / SIB.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.CyberlinkedTip: Cyberlinked controls: +2 to control / maneuver / weapon rolls. ACPA are normally linked.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.WeaponFireTip: Fire this weapon at the target (to-hit roll → resolver)
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.WeaponAddTip: Create a blank weapon to edit.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.WeaponsDragNote: Drag weapons from the Vehicle Weapons (MM) compendium onto this sheet, or add a blank one and edit it.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SystemAddTip: Create a blank system to edit.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SystemsDragNote: Drag systems from the ACPA Systems (MM) compendium onto this sheet, or add a blank one. (Offensive weapons use the Vehicle Weapons (MM) compendium.)
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.TotalCostTip: Total build cost — chassis + armor shell + Reality Interface + Reflex/Control + Command Computer + systems.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.WeightCapTip: Total loaded weight vs the chassis Lift/Capacity. An overweight suit is flagged below.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.LegalBuild: ✓ Legal build — within SP, weight, and space limits.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.AcpaFootnote: Powered armor (ACPA). The full build system — Linear Frame & Toughness, Reality Interface, Reflex/Control, derived SIB, per-area frame SOP, the systems catalog (per-system SOP), and the point-buy budget validator — and combat (Penetration damage, the System Hit / Critical Hit chart, melee) are in place.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.VehicleFootnote: Set the actor image (top-left) to your vehicle art, then drag the actor onto the canvas like any other actor — the token is pre-sized and scales to fit (drag its resize handle to adjust). Crew tokens placed on top render above it and ride along once boarded. Weapon mounts and the damage resolver arrive in later phases.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.WClassTip: Resolution archetype. Direct-fire = guns; Burst = HE/HEAT shells; Rocket = unguided HE; Missile = guided; Artillery = indirect; Bomb; Cone = scatter-packs; Melee = ACPA; Special.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.WMountTip: Weapon mount (MM p.15). Turret = 360°/+2 to-hit; Fixed = forward only; Articulated = one side; Open/Pintle = exposed; Pod; Jury-rigged.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.WArcTip: Firing arc relative to the vehicle's facing.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.WATip: Weapon Accuracy: a flat modifier to the to-hit roll (MM stat block).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.PenetrationTip: Vehicle Penetration — the parenthetical (n) in the MM stat block. Given directly by the book; compared to the target's Armor Value.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.DamageDiceTip: Personnel damage dice (e.g. 9D10). Used for the MM p.8 alternative method vs characters.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.FlagAPTip: Armor-piercing: ×2 Penetration Factor (already baked into the listed Pen for AP weapons).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.FlagHEATTip: HEAT / shaped-charge: Penetration is NOT affected by range; Composite Armor halves Pen (penetrating damage is not halved).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.FlagHiExTip: High-explosive: Penetration is not affected by range.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.HiDensityAPTip: High-density AP (errata p.105): full damage through armor, like HEAT (e.g. Barret 20mm, 30mm Gatling).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.BurstMTip: Burst radius in meters (0 = no area effect). Hi-Ex/HEAT shells, rockets, GLs, mortars, bombs.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ROFTip: Rate of fire. ROF 30 hits with 5 rounds per hit, ROF 100 with 10 (extra rounds add Penetration).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ROFAltTip: Alternate ROF for variable weapons (e.g. '30 OR 5'). 0 = none.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.MinRangeTip: Minimum range in meters (missiles = 1/10 Long range; 0 = none).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.GuidanceTip: Missile guidance: Semi-active uses the operator's skill; Active uses the missile's own Skill (ignores operator); Paint hits 2-10 if a painting laser hits.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.GuideSkillTip: Active missile's own Skill rating (e.g. +15 / +20), used in place of the operator's skill.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.HomingTip: Homing method — determines which countermeasures defeat it (radar ← chaff/jamming/ECM; thermal/IR ← flares/IR-baffling/IR-smoke; optical ← smoke; laser ← anti-laser aerosol).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ConeAngleTip: Cone angle in degrees for scatter-pack weapons (60 / 120 / 180).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ProjectilesTip: Number of projectiles per volley (cone/scatter weapons).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.ShellVariantsHint: Offered when firing. The warhead drives the effect: HEAT (shaped charge, halved by composite), WP (3D6 burn), Cluster (×3 burst, Pen 4), Chemical (gas cloud, no Pen). Leave empty for a plain HE round.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SysBodyAreaTip: Body area this system is mounted in. Destroying that area's frame knocks out its systems (Maximum Metal p.61).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SysMountTip: Internal = enclosed, protected by the suit armor. External = NOT armor-protected (carries its own SP). Either / Retract per the catalog.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SysSpacesTip: Spaces this system consumes in its body area (internal or external space budget, Maximum Metal p.61).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SysSPTip: Intrinsic Stopping Power (external / retractable items have their own SP).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SysSOPTip: Structural points — the system is destroyed when its accumulated SOP damage reaches this. 0 = derive 3× SP (Maximum Metal p.62).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SysWeightKgTip: Weight (kg) — counts toward total loaded weight for the SIB.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SysCostEbTip: Cost (eb) — counts toward the build budget.
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SysSOPDamageTip: Accumulated SOP damage from hits to this system (0 = undamaged).
CYBERPUNK.Vehicle.SysDestroyedTip: This system is destroyed (its SOP was exceeded). Set automatically by the damage resolver; editable for field repairs.
CYBERPUNK.OnlyProgramsCanBeActivated: Only programs can be activated. This is not a program: {name}
CYBERPUNK.NotEnoughRAM: Not enough free RAM to load “{name}” — {used}/{max} MU already in use.

CYBERPUNK.CWT_SkillNotFound: Skill not found on this actor
CYBERPUNK.CWT_SkillAmbiguous: Multiple matches found: {{count}}. Please be more specific.
CYBERPUNK.CWT_NoActorForSkills: No actor context: open this item from a character sheet to pick from their skills.
CYBERPUNK.SDPSumTooltip: Total SDP from implants and modules in this hit location
CYBERPUNK.SDPCurrentTooltip: Editable field for tracking SDP damage
CYBERPUNK.OnlyChipsHere: Only chips can be placed here.
CYBERPUNK.ImplantCannotBeInstalledInThis: The implant cannot be installed in this zone.
SETTINGS.FumbleTableEnabledHint: If enabled, whenever a skill check rolls a natural 1, the result is also determined using the fumble table.
SETTINGS.AutomationNoticeHide: Hide the Setup / What's New notice
SETTINGS.AutomationNoticeHideHint: When checked, the Cyberpunk 2020 setup & what's-new dialog stops appearing on load for the GM. Uncheck to see it again. (The notice's own 'Don't show this again' checkbox sets this too.)
SETTINGS.PlayersCanBuyAmmoHint: When off, only the GM can buy ammo; players are told they must purchase it at a shop and should ask the GM. Keeps ammo from appearing out of thin air.
SETTINGS.AmmoLockerEnabledHint: Optional, off by default. When on, any miscellaneous item can be turned into an 'Ammo Locker' (an in-inventory button that opens the ammo purchasing dialog). Leave off to buy ammo from the shop catalog's Ammo section instead.
SETTINGS.AmmoBlackhandsBoxes: Use Blackhand's Guide ammo box sizes
SETTINGS.AmmoBlackhandsBoxesHint: Optional. Switches firearm ammunition to Blackhand's Guide's uniform box-of-100 pricing instead of the Core rulebook's per-class box sizes. Default off (Core).
SETTINGS.AmmoBlackhandsBrassHint: Optional. Brass-cased loads cost x3 the base price (Blackhand's Guide) instead of x2 (Core rulebook). Default off (Core).
SETTINGS.ShoppingEnabledHint: Master toggle for the Shopping feature. When on, a 'Shop' button appears on character sheets and shops/purchases become available. Off by default (opt-in).
SETTINGS.PlayersCanShopHint: When off, only the GM can buy; players are directed to ask the GM. Keeps gear from appearing out of thin air.
SETTINGS.ShopBuySourceHint: What players can buy from when buying directly: the full catalog (all compendia), or only shops the GM has published.
SETTINGS.ShopAllowHomebrewHint: Off by default. When on, community / non-canon / cross-system items become available in the shop, where the GM can enable individual sources for players. Core and official R.Talsorian books are unaffected by this.
SETTINGS.ShopShowSource: Show item sources in the shop
SETTINGS.ShopShowSourceHint: Show a small badge on each shop item naming the book/source it comes from. Per-user — turn it off if you prefer cleaner rows.
SETTINGS.IpSystemHint: Off by default (free skill editing). Simple = one IP pool per character. RAW = the full per-skill Improvement Points tracker (GM-attributed awards, banked-per-skill, self-service level-ups).
SETTINGS.IpAwardModelHint: Manual = the GM types IP per skill use (RAW). Auto baseline = the GM ticks success on a queued roll and a fixed IP is granted automatically (the GM can still add bonus IP).
SETTINGS.IpAutoBaselineAmountHint: IP granted per GM-marked success when the award model is Auto baseline.
SETTINGS.IpThrottleHint: Optional secondary cap on farming one skill. Off = GM polices manually (default). Hard cap = one award per skill per Apply cycle. Diminishing = each further award on the same skill this cycle is halved.
SETTINGS.IpSkillLockModeHint: Who controls the skill-lock that prevents hand-editing skill levels/IP (rolling and confirm-button level-ups always work). Owner = the player. GM = the GM only. Mutual = a player soft-lock plus a GM hard-lock the player can't override.
SETTINGS.IpShowPendingHint: Show the GM-only “pending IP” pip on skill rows (pending IP is hidden from players until applied). Per-user.
SETTINGS.DamageArmorModeHint: How armor SP is applied when calculating damage. Full = SP + ablation per RAW. Simple = SP subtracted, no ablation. None = armor ignored (BTM still applies).
SETTINGS.DamageAblationHint: When enabled, armor SP at the hit location is reduced by 1 for each penetrating hit (RAW).
SETTINGS.DamageAutoApplyHint: When enabled, damage is applied to the target immediately when a targeted weapon fires, without showing the confirmation dialog.
SETTINGS.AutoRangefindingHint: When enabled, the range category (Point Blank / Close / Medium / Long / Extreme) is automatically determined from the distance between the attacking and target tokens on the canvas, using the scene's configured distance units. The attack modifier is set accordingly. Requires a targeted token.
SETTINGS.ReputationEnabledHint: Show the Reputation panel on the Combat tab (a GM-set Rep score, plus Facedown and Recognition roll buttons). Facedown = both sides roll 1d10 + COOL + Reputation; the loser backs down or is at −3 vs that foe until they win a Facedown against them (CP2020 p.54). Turn off to hide it for tables that don't use Reputation.
SETTINGS.HeadHitDoublingHint: When enabled, a hit to the Head doubles the FINAL damage — after armor (SP) and BTM are applied. RAW: 'A head hit always doubles damage' (CP2020 p.103, the optional 'He Shrugs Off Head Hits' rule); the book gives no timing, so the wound that actually gets through is what doubles. Disable for groups that skip this rule.
SETTINGS.LimbLossEnabled: Combat: Limb Loss & Head Wound Checks
SETTINGS.LimbLossEnabledHint: When enabled, a single hit dealing more than 8 net damage to a limb triggers an immediate Death Save at Mortal 0 (severed/crushed). A head wound of the same severity kills automatically (CP2020 p.103 RAW).
SETTINGS.SuppressiveFireSavesHint: When enabled, suppressive fire automatically places a ray template (fire zone) on the canvas and prompts all tokens within it to roll an Evasion check: Athletics + REF + 1d10 vs DC = rounds / zone width (CP2020 p.101 RAW). Failures take 1d6 random hits.
SETTINGS.AutoDeathSavePerTurnHint: When enabled, unstabilized Mortal characters are automatically prompted to make a Death Save at the start of each of their turns in the combat tracker (CP2020 p.105 RAW).
SETTINGS.AutoSaveRePrompt: Combat: Stun Save Recovery Each Turn
SETTINGS.AutoSaveRePromptHint: When enabled, unconscious/stunned characters are automatically prompted to roll a Stun Save recovery check at the start of each of their turns in the combat tracker (CP2020 p.104 RAW).
SETTINGS.LayerRuleSystemHint: Core (CP2020 p.99 errata New Rule 1): max 3 layers, max 1 hard per location, EV +1/+2 for 2nd/3rd layer. Chromebook 4 (CB4 p.67): clothing weight categories (Light/Medium/Heavy) with separate EV penalties for over-layering by body area (Torso vs Legs). The two systems are mutually exclusive.
SETTINGS.ApplyLayerEVPenalty: Armor: Apply Layer EV Penalties (New Rule 1)
SETTINGS.ApplyLayerEVPenaltyHint: When enabled, the 2nd armor layer at any location adds +1 EV and the 3rd adds an additional +2 EV to the REF penalty (CP2020 errata New Rule 1). Skinweave receives no penalty.
SETTINGS.ActiveDodgeParryEnabledHint: When enabled, 🛡 Dodge and ⛨ Parry buttons appear in the combat tracker. Dodge (active combatant): −2 to attacker's melee roll this round; clears on next turn. Parry (any combatant, reactive): blocks the next incoming melee attack; consumed on use. (CP2020 p.102 RAW.)
SETTINGS.AimTrackingEnabledHint: When enabled, a Take Aim (🎯) button appears in the combat tracker for the active combatant. Each click accumulates +1 aim round (max 3) stored on the actor. The attack modifier dialog is automatically pre-filled with the saved aim count. Aim resets when the actor fires. (CP2020 p.99 RAW: +1 per consecutive aim round, max +3.)
SETTINGS.WaitForTurnEnabledHint: When enabled, a Wait (⏸) button appears in the combat tracker for the active combatant. Clicking it sets their initiative just below the current minimum and advances to the next combatant, so they act last this round. Since CP2020 re-rolls initiative each round, this is a temporary deferral. (CP2020 p.98 RAW.)
SETTINGS.SpecialMeleeEffectsEnabled: Combat: Martial Arts Special Hit Effects
SETTINGS.SpecialMeleeEffectsEnabledHint: When enabled, successful Hold/Grapple attacks set a status flag on the target with turn-start reminders; Choke deals 1d6 HP damage per turn + forces a Stun Save; Throw/Sweep post knockdown announcements; Escape removes all hold/grapple/choke flags. (CP2020 p.100–102 RAW.)
SETTINGS.GasGrenadeCloudEnabled: Combat: Gas Grenade Cloud & Per-Turn Saves
SETTINGS.GasGrenadeCloudEnabledHint: When enabled, weapons loaded with gas ammo (effectTypes: ['Gas'] on ammo item) place a green circle MeasuredTemplate on the canvas. All tokens within the cloud are prompted to make Stun Saves each turn. Cloud persists for dotTurns turns then auto-deletes. (CP2020 p.107 area weapon rules.)
SETTINGS.GasCloudAutoMoveHint: When enabled, the gas cloud template drifts 2m in a random direction each turn to simulate wind movement (CP2020 p.107). When disabled, the GM may reposition the template manually.
SETTINGS.TaserCumPenaltyEnabledHint: When enabled, each successive taser hit within a 3-turn window reduces the target's Stun Save threshold by the ammo item's stunSaveMod value (default −2 per hit). The penalty accumulates: 2nd hit −2, 3rd hit −4, etc. (CP2020 p.101 RAW.)
SETTINGS.AcidArmorDotEnabledHint: When enabled, weapons loaded with acid ammo (dotEnabled on ammo item) degrade the target's armor SP at the hit location by the dotDamageFormula roll (default 1d6) per turn for dotTurns turns. SP is reduced from the outermost layer inward. (CP2020 acid weapon rules.)
SETTINGS.AcidDotStackModeHint: Controls what happens when a target is hit by acid while an acid effect is already active. Stack: extends the remaining turns at the same location. Reset: overwrites the previous effect (timer restarts). Separate: both effects run concurrently with independent timers.
SETTINGS.FireDotEnabledHint: When enabled, weapons loaded with incendiary/API ammo set the target on fire: the dotDamageFormula roll (default 1d6) is applied as HP damage at the hit location each turn for dotTurns turns, with a Stun Save each turn. Unlike acid, fire burns the target, not their armor.
SETTINGS.FireDotStackModeHint: Controls what happens when a target is set on fire while already burning. Stack: extends the remaining turns at the same location. Reset: overwrites the previous fire (timer restarts). Separate: both fires run concurrently with independent timers.
SETTINGS.MultiActionPenaltyEnabledHint: When enabled, each action taken beyond the first in a round applies a cumulative −3 penalty to all rolls that round. A badge in the combat tracker shows the current action count and live penalty. (CP2020 p.105 RAW.)
SETTINGS.MultiActionAutoTrackHint: When enabled, weapon fire and tracker button clicks (Aim, Dodge, Parry) automatically increment the action counter. When disabled, only the manual ➕ button in the tracker changes the count — useful for tables that prefer full manual control.
SETTINGS.DamageLayersEnabledHint: Displays a per-location armor layer summary on the Combat tab, showing layer order, hard/soft classification, RAW limit warnings (max 3 layers, max 1 hard), and extra EV penalties per New Rule 1.
SETTINGS.CyberpsychosisTrackingHint: Derives a cyberpsychosis state from the character's current Empathy (after humanity loss from cyberware): EMP 3 = cold, 2 = withdrawn, 1 = sociopathic, 0 or less = cyberpsycho (CP2020 p.73). Shown on the Cyberware tab. Humanity loss itself is always tracked; this only controls the derived state readout.
SETTINGS.LimbCripplingDetailedHint: Optional grittier limb rule from Listen Up You Primitive Screwheads. Limb damage is DOUBLED (post-armor, before BTM); 6–12 net to a limb cripples it (unusable), 13+ destroys it (needs replacement). Replaces the Core flat '>8 = severed' limb branch when on. Requires 'Limb Loss & Head Wound Checks' to be enabled. Default OFF (Core rules).
SETTINGS.HitLocationCoreDisplayHint: When on (default), the chat shows which body part each hit struck, using the standard Core rulebook chart (head, torso, arms, legs). Can't be combined with W4RST4R's Limb Rules, which has its own chart — turning that model on switches this off.
SETTINGS.W4rst4rLimbRules: Combat: W4RST4R's Limb Rules (alternate limb model)
SETTINGS.W4rst4rLimbRulesHint: An alternate set of limb-injury rules. When a single hit deals more than 8 damage to an arm or leg the limb is disabled; more than 12 severs it — in either case the character must make a Death Save to survive. A head hit over 8 is instantly fatal. It also uses its own hit-location chart that adds the groin. Turning this on replaces the standard limb rules. Default OFF.
SETTINGS.ShotgunSpreadEnabledHint: When enabled, ammo whose Spread Mode is not 'single' (buckshot, flechette) fires a widening pattern (Close 1m/Med 2m/Long 3m by default) with range-banded damage. Everyone in the straight path takes the hit. Only affects ammo explicitly configured for spread, so normal weapons are unchanged. (CP2020 p.108.)
SETTINGS.ExplosivesEnabledHint: When enabled, ammo whose Effect Types include 'Explosive' detonates as an area-effect blast: a circular zone of radius blastRadius, with range-banded damage falloff (blastMultipliers) outward from the center. Every token in the blast takes damage through the normal pipeline. Only affects ammo configured as Explosive. (CP2020 p.108.)
SETTINGS.AreaEffectOcclusionHint: When enabled, a token shielded by a wall between it and the blast center (or the shooter, for spread) is exempt from area-effect damage — intervening cover blocks the pattern/blast (CP2020 p.108). Requires walls placed on the scene; disable if your tables don't map cover with walls.
SETTINGS.VehicleControlEnabledHint: When enabled, vehicles get a 🎲 Control Roll button (sheet header) and the game.cyberpunk.vehicles.controlRoll API. It opens a dialog to roll REF + Driving/Pilot + 1d10 vs a Difficulty Value (Simple 15 / Difficult 20 / Very Difficult 25), and on failure rolls the Control Loss (Core p.112) or Failure (Maximum Metal p.10) table — whichever the active ruleset selects. Works in Core mode without Maximum Metal. Default ON.
SETTINGS.VehicleDamageEnabledHint: When enabled, vehicles get a 💥 Damage button (sheet header) and the game.cyberpunk.vehicles.applyDamage API. Core (p.112) subtracts SP and reduces SDP; Maximum Metal (p.4-6) compares Penetration to Armor Value, rolls the Surface/Minor/Major/Catastrophic damage table, then a hit location with fuel-fire / ammo-cookoff / crew-damage effects (and honors a Damage Control system). The active branch follows the ruleset (Core when Maximum Metal is off). Default ON.
SETTINGS.MmEnabledHint: Master switch for the Maximum Metal military-hardware layer. When OFF (default), vehicles use only the Core 'Vehicles in FNFF' rules (CP2020 p.112) and every MM-only feature is disabled: the Penetration/Armor-Value resolver, composite armor, personnel-vs-anti-vehicle (p.8), area weapons, missiles, the 5-facing vehicle sheet, and the Maximum Metal weapon compendium seeding. Turn ON for the detailed military system. The settings below belong to Maximum Metal.
SETTINGS.VehicleRuleSystemHint: Core = the simple Vehicles-in-FNFF rules (Control Roll vs DV 15/20/25, SP−SDP damage, crash = speed/20 × weight). Maximum Metal = the detailed military system (Penetration vs Armor Value, Surface/Minor/Major/Catastrophic damage, hit-location & crit tables, ACPA). The vehicle sheet shows a single SP in Core mode and all five facings under Maximum Metal.
SETTINGS.VehicleArmorDamageEnabled: Maximum Metal: Armor Damage via Penetration (errata)
SETTINGS.VehicleArmorDamageEnabledHint: Optional errata rule (Maximum Metal p.107). A heavy round (>20mm) erodes the struck facing's SP whether or not it penetrates: SP removed = factor × Penetration (HE ×½, AP/DPU ×0.6, HEAT ×¾, HESH ×1.0). Because Armor Value is derived from SP (SP÷20), sustained fire grinds armor down over time — addressing 'hard to knock down' heavy armor. Applies only under the Maximum Metal resolver. Default OFF; intended for >20mm vehicle weapons (the GM enables it deliberately).
SETTINGS.VehicleMoraleEnabledHint: Optional rule. After a vehicle takes a Minor-or-worse penetrating hit, its crew must pass a morale check — Leadership + 1d10 vs 15 — or bail out / disengage. The damage card shows the 1d10 result and the Leadership needed to hold; the GM adjudicates the consequence. Applies only under the Maximum Metal resolver. Default OFF.
SETTINGS.VehicleArcEnforcementHint: How a weapon mount's firing arc (turret 360° / front / side / rear) is enforced when the target lies outside it. Token facing defines 'front' — rotate a vehicle with Ctrl+scroll (Foundry's 0° points north). Free (default): the Fire dialog only WARNS that the target is outside the mount's arc; you can still fire (GM discretion). Strict: an out-of-arc shot is blocked until the mount can bear — rotate the firing vehicle to face the target, or use a turret. Applies to all vehicle/ACPA weapon mounts, missiles included.
SETTINGS.VehicleArcEnforcementChoiceStri: Strict (block out-of-arc shots — keep mounts within bounds)
SETTINGS.ExplosivesDetailed: Combat: Detailed Explosives — HEP Concussion (Listen Up)
SETTINGS.ExplosivesDetailedHint: Optional grittier blast model from Listen Up You Primitive Screwheads (p.105). Explosion concussion is treated as HEP: armor SP does NOT protect (BTM still applies), half the damage that gets through is permanent and half is stun (a Stun Save is always prompted), and soft armor at the hit location loses 2 SP. If the ammo also has blastShrapnel, each target additionally takes a normal-armor 1d10 shrapnel hit. Default OFF (Core blast = damage through normal armor).

CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.Title: Reflex (Combat)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just screw up.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.6: 6. Weapon discharges or strikes something harmless.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.7: 7. Weapon jams, or knocks you to the ground for 1 round.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.9_10: 9–10. You manage to wound a member of your own party.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.Title: Reflex (Athletics)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just mess up and make an idiot of yourself.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.5_7: 5–7. You fail miserably. Take 1 point in minor damage (sprain, fall, stumble), plus make a Save vs. Stun.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.8_10: 8–10. You fail abysmally. If a physical action, take 1D6 in damage from falling or strained muscles. Also make a roll vs Stun at -1.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.Title: Control Loss Table
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.1_2: 1–2. Skid or slew; no other result.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.3_4.Ground: 3–4. Major skid; slide 1D10x10 feet sideways in direction of travel.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.3_4.Aircraf: 3–4. Aircraft stalls, losing 1D10x50 feet of altitude.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.5_6.Ground: 5–6. Roll ground vehicle after sliding 1D10x10 feet sideways in direction of travel; take 5D6 damage.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.5_6.Aircraf: 5–6. Aircraft goes into spin, lose 1D10x100 feet of altitude.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.Title: Tech (Repair or create)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just can't get it together.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.5_7: 5–7. You not only fail, you make it worse! You drop the tools you're working with, or you lose your grip and damage the thing you're working with even more. Raise the Difficulty by 5 points and try again.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.8_10: 8–10. Wow. Did you ever blow it! You damaged the device or creation beyond repair. Buy a new one.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.Title: EMP (Convince, Fast talk, Seduce)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. They just won't buy it.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.5_6: 5–6. So much for your people skills. You not only don't convince them; you leave them totally cold (-4 to your next EMP die roll) to any other suggestion you might have.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.7_10: 7–10. Yow! You blew it royally. You not only didn't convince them, but now they're actually violently opposed to anything you want to do. Roll 1D10. On a 1–4, they actually attempt to do you physical harm.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.EmpExtra.1_4: they actually attempt to do you physical harm.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.EmpExtra.5_10: they are violently opposed and resist you.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.Title: INT (Figure out, Notice, catch a clue)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just don't know how to do it. You don't know what's going on. You carry on, oblivious to higher concerns.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.5_7: 5–7. You don't know anything about what's going on and you haven't a clue about how to do anything about it. Make a Convince check at -2 to see if anyone else notices how dumb you are.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.8_10: 8–10. Wow, are you oblivious. You not only don't know what's going on or anything about the subject, but everyone knows how ignorant you are.
